note: Adult (>=50 kg, no organ impairment) outpatient daily-dose ceilings, mg/day. Advisory only — the aggregation flag is a prompt to check the combined molecule load across co-prescribed products, not a hard contraindication. Seed set = paracetamol + the NSAIDs and decongestant stimulants that recur in Indian fever/pain combination brands. Extend as needed; molecules without a ceiling here are still aggregated but never flagged.

limits.caution_note: Consider a 3 g/day ceiling in the elderly, low body weight (<50 kg), chronic alcohol use, or hepatic impairment.
limits.note: Hepatotoxicity above the daily ceiling; the commonest stacking risk when a scheduled antipyretic (e.g. Dolo 650) is combined with a paracetamol-containing NSAID combo (e.g. Zerodol-SP, Sinarest).

limits.caution_note: OTC/self-medication ceiling is 1200 mg/day; 2400 mg is the prescription maximum.
limits.note: GI and renal risk; use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.
100 mg twice daily is the standard maximum.
150 mg/day oral maximum; cardiovascular risk is dose-related.
1000 mg/day maintenance maximum (1250 mg only for the first day of acute use).
120 mg/day is reserved for acute gout, short term; 90 mg/day for most other indications.
500 mg three times daily maximum; limit to 7 days.
From combination analgesics/migraine products; excludes dietary caffeine, which adds to the total.
Oral decongestant daily maximum (10 mg up to 6 times/day).
